clue.text: Well heated, for a hovel

parts.note: for can mean to, as in a present for or to someone
a sty is a filthy hovel, as well as a pig's pen

explanation.surface: An odd recommendation that a shack be kept nicely warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like it names the thing being warmed, but each of its three words supplies letters in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something toasty is pleasantly warm, as if just in front of the fire.

clue.text: Speaker's pretty terse before start of speech

parts.note: twee means affectedly pretty or quaint

indicators.note: only the part of the word terse that comes before its letter S, the opening letter of speech, is kept

explanation.surface: Someone's speaking style is described as sweetly curt until they actually start talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before start of speech' keeps only the letters of terse that come before the S beginning 'speech'. 'Speaker' is a loudspeaker, not a talker; the 's is a link (is).
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is the small loudspeaker in a hi-fi that handles the high frequencies.

clue.text: Creature with shell, or hard top, alternatively

indicators.note: alternatively suggests the letters of the phrase or hard top arranged another way

explanation.surface: Describing an animal protected either by a shell or a hard cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link offering a choice but belongs to the anagram fodder with 'hard top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthropods such as crabs and insects have a hard exoskeleton, a shell-like outer casing.

clue.text: Class of thirty cleared out before tiring lesson

indicators.note: the word thirty is emptied of its inner letters, leaving only its ends

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the school lesson that tires pupils out

explanation.surface: A class of thirty pupils is emptied of the room ahead of an exhausting lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind or category, the same as a class of things.

clue.text: Rabbits changing hands as property

indicators.note: the right hand (R) is swapped for the left hand (L) in the word chatters

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for talking at length, so rabbits are chatters

explanation.surface: Pet rabbits sold on and passed between owners as belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbits' is a verb here, British for talks on and on; 'changing hands' swaps right (R) for left (L). 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattels are movable personal possessions, a legal term for goods and belongings.

clue.text: Actor that's annoying and creepy regularly scratched graffiti in the toilet

parts.note: humph is an exclamation of annoyance, as if saying that's annoying

indicators.note: taking every other letter of creepy, at regular intervals

parts.note: bog is British slang for toilet and graffiti scratched there is bog art

explanation.surface: Complaining about an irritating, creepy person who scrawled on the lavatory wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes R, E, Y from creepy. BOG is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was the Hollywood star of Casablanca and The Maltese Falcon.

clue.text: Worn-out type in this puzzle, with pop-up blocker installed?

indicators.note: installed means set inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the clue answered by type in this very crossword is 3-down, so this gives the number three
an ad bar would be something that blocks pop-up advertisements

explanation.surface: A worn-out computer setup gets a pop-up blocker installed.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPE is the answer to 3-down, so 'type in this puzzle' is THREE; 'installed' puts AD BAR inside it. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn so thin the threads show, hence shabby and used up.

clue.text: Parting words starting barely halfway through drunken voicemail

indicators.note: the run of letters begins just after the middle of drunken and runs on into voicemail, concealed inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A slurred voice message trails off midway, the last thing said.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short closing stanza of a poem, a parting address from the poet.

clue.text: Butcher reportedly pulled vehicle, helped by runners

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that is said out loud rather than spelt

parts.note: to butcher is to slay or slaughter

explanation.surface: A butcher is said to have hauled a cart along with the help of some runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is drawn by horses or reindeer and glides over snow on runners.

clue.text: Born Conservative admits evidence of male entitlement, writing about life

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: someone natural is born to a role, as in a born leader
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
his, as on matching his and hers towels, marks something belonging to a man

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a born Tory confesses to privileged male attitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural history is the study and description of living things, plants and animals.

clue.text: Cap broken mescal bottles in which the spirit leaks out

definitions.text: in which the spirit leaks out

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so one piece is contained by the other
broken means the letters of mescal are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A cracked mescal bottle cap lets the liquor seep out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles the drink's name to ECLASM, and 'bottles' holds the cap inside. 'spirit' looks like the drink; it is a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance said by spiritualists to stream from a medium as a ghost materialises.

clue.text: Show minister Uxbridge, where there's a vacancy

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion

indicators.note: the word Uxbridge is vacated, emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: Pointing a minister to Uxbridge, a London suburb, where a post is open.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a stage show of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Horse-racing windfall leaving one taken aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
leaving means one goes away, taken out of the word

parts.note: a windfall is fruit blown down from a tree
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lucky win at the races disappears, leaving someone stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windfall' is a fallen apple, not a lucky win: FRUIT less I is FRUT, which 'taken aback' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: The turf is a name for horse racing as a sport, after the grass courses.

clue.text: Direction of U-boat maybe a secondary issue

parts.note: a U-boat is an example of a sub, a submarine
a heading is the direction a vessel steers

explanation.surface: The course of a German submarine treated as a side matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A subheading is a lesser title under a main one, so a subsidiary topic.

clue.text: Jugular nerve out of order, a constriction

indicators.note: out of order means the two pieces appear in the clue the other way round from the answer

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
the jugular is the great vein of the neck, so the neck stands for it

explanation.surface: A medical note on a disordered nerve in the throat that narrows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' says the clue gives NECK and BOTTLE swapped. BOTTLE is British for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrow point that holds up flow, like the slim neck of a bottle.

clue.text: Unprincipled soldiers given test of will

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
probate is the legal process proving that a will is valid

explanation.surface: Morally loose troops are put through a trial of resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' looks like willpower; it is a legal testament. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate person is depraved, without moral scruples; the word is used as an adjective here.

clue.text: Husband joins club; a wife's place?

indicators.note: joins means the two pieces are attached side by side

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sports

explanation.surface: A man signs up for a club, leaving the question of where his wife belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wife of Bath is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims; Bath is an English spa city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Wife of Bath takes her title from the city she comes from.

clue.text: Thieves duck where icicles hang down

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
icicles form hanging from the eaves of a roof

explanation.surface: Robbers crouch beneath the overhanging roof edge in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang for thief. 'duck' looks like a verb (stoop) but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang tea leaf means thief, so the plural stands for robbers.

clue.text: Improve by cutting what you eat, putting energy first

indicators.note: the letter for energy, E, is shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: your diet is what you eat

explanation.surface: Advice on slimming: cut back on food but prioritise energy.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the physics symbol for energy, moved from the end of DIET to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it, often by removing material to sharpen it.

clue.text: Hurry round capital city, costing sleep

indicators.note: round means going around, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning hurry
Bern is the capital of Switzerland
at can mean costing, as in apples at a pound

explanation.surface: Rushing round an expensive capital costs a traveller their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To hibernate is to pass the winter in a dormant, sleep-like state.

clue.text: Fair sex denied vote, daughter found out

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition or trade fair

indicators.note: denied means deprived of, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made when voting

explanation.surface: Women denied the vote, and a daughter discovers the injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair sex' looks like one phrase meaning women; it splits into a trade fair and SEX, which loses its X.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exposed has been unmasked, their secret revealed.

clue.text: Jaw cold immediately after ice-lolly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
on can mean straight after, as in on arrival
Fab is a British brand of ice lolly

explanation.surface: Biting a frozen ice lolly makes your jaw feel cold right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaw' is a verb, chat; Fab is a British ice-lolly brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaw is informal for talk, and a confab is an informal chat.

clue.text: Fellows in some muddled advisory group disagreeing with the PM?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
muddled means mixed up, so the letters of some are jumbled

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, doubled for the plural
SAGE was the UK Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies during the pandemic

explanation.surface: A dig at a confused government advisory panel at odds with the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' turns SOME into OME, with FF put in it; SAGE advised the UK government on Covid.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians off-message stray from the party line set by the leader.

clue.text: Paper to do origami missing last two bits

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: origami is the art of paper folding, so to do it is to fold
binary bits are 1 and 0, which look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Instructions to fold a sheet for origami, minus the last couple of steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' are binary digits, 1 and 0, read as I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet of paper folded once, or a book page size made from one.

clue.text: Hard to fathom?

parts.note: hard to understand, and also hard to sound with a line marked in fathoms because the water goes so far down

explanation.surface: A puzzling thing that cannot be understood.
explanation.walkthrough: A fathom is a six-foot unit for measuring water depth, so the phrase works literally as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profound is hard to grasp, and deep water is hard to measure.

clue.text: One-one; close

parts.note: one as a pronoun stands for oneself, so for me
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tight score in a match, one goal each.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is not near: it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Close is an old-fashioned word for stingy, tight-fisted with money.

clue.text: Logical result of Cornish river and home counties being adjacent?

indicators.note: adjacent means next to each other, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the home counties around London lie in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: A wry query about whether Cornwall touches the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is far from the home counties, so the claim is indeed untrue, a nice &lit-ish touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic a proposition evaluates to true or untrue; untrue is called this.

clue.text: Solver Sue's beaten us emphatically

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so the letters of solver Sue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver named Sue has beaten us at the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link (has).
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun adds emphasis to we or us, as in we did it by ourselves.

clue.text: Borough of Hamlyn cut in two by beck

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the pieces side by side

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a brook

indicators.note: the word Hamlyn is halved and only its back half used

explanation.surface: A town in the north split in half by a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut in two' keeps the second half, LYN, of Hamlyn.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: Journalist follows university students straight out of the factory

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so this piece goes at the end

parts.note: NUS is the UK National Union of Students
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter trails college students leaving a works.
explanation.definitionFit: Unused goods are brand new, never handled since they were made.
